calls.video_title: Why These 5 Stocks Are Crashing (But I'm Buying More)
calls.thesis: FLIP: last stance HOLD (after the Q3 disappointment, when he stopped adding). 'I stay bullish on him and hers' — shares now ~$14, below even the level at the Novo Nordisk lawsuit bottom. Revenue has compounded 64% over almost 5 years, with ~50% growth expected in H2 2026 partly from acquisitions, and the enterprise value is just $4B at 1.4x sales. He uses its labs himself and calls the platform the right way to disrupt healthcare; the risk-reward is 'exactly what I want as an investor'.
calls.base: The platform keeps compounding and the 1.4x sales multiple re-rates.
calls.bull: Peptides and the early-2027 weight-loss platform launch re-accelerate growth.
calls.bear: Margin compression and branded-product pricing pressure persist.

calls.thesis: Stance flip BUY (3 Nov) -> HOLD: after a disappointing Q3, he is NOT selling his shares and still calls Hims & Hers a great company to own over 5-10 years, but he is no longer adding — subscriber count fell ~100k QoQ, gross margin compressed 83% to 57% on the shift to branded GLP-1s, Q4 revenue guidance is slightly down vs Q3, full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut, management skipped its usual 2030 guidance and earnings presentation. He says management has to answer the questions over the next handful of quarters.
calls.price_at_call: shares down ~18% after earnings, ~40% over the past month
calls.base_case: Long-term subscription-health / Costco model works: TRT and peptides (launching late Nov, made in-house in the US) re-accelerate customer growth in early 2027.
calls.bull_case: Peptides and TRT scale fast, Huberman board/adviser push lands, Hims becomes the platform that owns the customer relationship in a $400B+ pharma market.
calls.bear_case: Subscriber declines continue, competition from Ro/Amazon and small players overwhelms the model, peptide execution stumbles, or Q1 2027 guidance disappoints.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (prior BUY 10 Oct): calls Hims & Hers extremely undervalued and a potential 100x over 10-20 years, despite the stock down 38% over the past year and 8.2% in the past month. Five reasons: a huge US pharma market ($400-800B), market leadership (51% of observed telehealth sales, 48.5% of customers vs Ro/Roman ~23-25%), expanding specialties (dermatology, mental health, hormone health, weight loss, now testosterone/TRT), international expansion (Germany, Canada, Australia via Eucalyptus, Japan potential), and peptides as a new leg (in-house compounding facility, HHS draft interim policy opening BPC-157/TB500, modelled at $180M at 100k subscribers, $1.8B at 1M).
calls.price_at_call: ~$6.4B market cap; ~$2.6B revenue, H2 2026 guidance +50% YoY
calls.base_case: Revenue grows toward $5-6B in a couple of years on peptides plus organic/GLP-1 momentum, justifying a much higher multiple than near-1x sales.
calls.bull_case: 100x over 10-20 years if it becomes a top-2/3 player in a massive disrupted market.
calls.bear_case: International expansion adds execution risk for management; peptides still need final rules written; Q3 earnings due 9 Nov are the near-term catalyst.

calls.thesis: GLP-1 compounding disruption settled (Novo/Eli Lilly products now on platform); guidance of 50% revenue growth in H2 2026 after Eucalyptus/Zava acquisitions; EV/sales ~2.8 with a ~$400B+ pharma TAM to attack.
